user_prompt: What is the effect of exercise training (aerobic, resistance, combined or other structured exercise, delivered during or between dialysis sessions), compared with no exercise or a placebo exercise (such as stretching or sham exercise), on lower-limb functional strength measured by the sit-to-stand test in adults receiving maintenance dialysis (haemodialysis or peritoneal dialysis)?  Effect measure: pool as a mean difference (MD) in seconds using a random-effects model. MD < 0 means a shorter time (better performance) with exercise (favours exercise). Report the difference as exercise minus control.  Outcome: the time in seconds to complete five repetitions of the sit-to-stand test, extracted as the mean, SD and number of participants per arm. - Use the five-repetition (or five to ten repetition) timed sit-to-stand test, where the result is a time in seconds. Do not use the 30-second or 60-second test, where the result is a count of repetitions in a fixed time, and do not use the timed up-and-go or six-minute walk test. - Use the end-of-intervention value (mean and SD). If a trial reports only the change from baseline (mean change and SD of change), use those for both arms and state it. Do not mix an end value in one arm with a change score in the other. - If a trial reports several time points during the intervention, use the one at the end of the exercise programme. Do not use follow-up after the programme ended. - If variability is reported as SE or SEM, convert to SD = SE × √n. Check table footnotes for whether "±" is SD or SE. - Convert times to seconds. If a paper reports the result as a number of repetitions per time, leave it out of this outcome. - Control: usual care or no exercise, or a placebo exercise. Exclude trials whose control group does a different active exercise or receives another active intervention. - Multi-arm and factorial trials: combine several exercise arms into one exercise group (pool means and SDs, sum participants), and combine several control arms into one control group, or take the arm that matches the question and state the choice. For trials with several exercise arms and one control group, use the control group once. - Use the number randomised or analysed as reported; assign arms by treatment description, not by column position. - Include only randomised controlled trials in adults on maintenance dialysis. Exclude kidney transplant recipients, people with non-dialysis kidney disease, and non-randomised studies. Theses and dissertations that report a randomised trial are eligible.  Do not pool the 30-second sit-to-stand count, blood pressure, quality of life, dialysis adequacy, adverse events or any non-sit-to-stand outcome.
